sense: going off: go away, run away

evidence: Plaut. Cas. 148: St! tacē atque abī.
Cic. Cat. 1.20: abīre in aliquās terrās (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin puts “away” into the verb, with ab- (ā-, abs-, au-): abīre, go away; auferre, take away (see remove); aufugere, run away; āvolāre, fly away (see fly away). Abī! is “go away!”, or, kindly, “off you go”.

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; apud Cicerōnem numquam
evidence: Plaut. Am. 2.1.32: apage tē ā mē (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek ἄπαγε; also “away with it!”, refusing something (see yucky).

phrases.english: Shh! Quiet, and off you go.

phrases.latin: Tacē atque abī intrō. — Taceō atque abeō.
phrases.english: Hush and go inside. — Hushing and going.

sources: Lewis & Short: abeo · Lewis & Short: apage · Lewis & Short: aufugio
